title: The elicited dismissal-policy determines whether a version bump re-surfaces the tour
asA: principal who dismissed the tour once on a project applying application-onboarding-tour
iWant: a subsequent tour version bump to re-surface the tour only if the elicited policy says so
soThat: a project's dismissal policy is the policy I actually experience across releases

acceptanceCriteria.description: When dismissal-policy is `dismiss-permanently` and the principal dismisses the tour, the completion record marks the dismissal terminal and no version bump re-opens the tour; only the restart-tour control clears the record and re-opens.
acceptanceCriteria.given: dismissal-policy=dismiss-permanently applied and the principal dismissed the tour once
acceptanceCriteria.when: the tour version bumps and the principal re-loads
acceptanceCriteria.then: the tour stays dismissed regardless of the version bump; the restart-tour control clears the record and re-opens the tour

acceptanceCriteria.description: When dismissal-policy is `dismiss-until-next-major` the completion store writes the dismissed tour's SemVer, and on principal load compares the stored major segment against the current tour's major segment; the tour re-opens iff the majors differ.
acceptanceCriteria.given: dismissal-policy=dismiss-until-next-major applied and a completion record from tour v1.4.2
acceptanceCriteria.then: a bump to v1.5.0 does not re-open the tour, a bump to v2.0.0 does re-open it

acceptanceCriteria.description: When dismissal-policy is `dismiss-until-next-minor` the completion store writes the dismissed tour's SemVer, and on principal load compares stored and current major.minor; the tour re-opens iff either segment differs.
acceptanceCriteria.given: dismissal-policy=dismiss-until-next-minor applied and a completion record from tour v1.4.2
acceptanceCriteria.then: a bump to v1.4.9 does not re-open the tour, a bump to v1.5.0 does re-open it and a bump to v2.0.0 does re-open it

acceptanceCriteria.description: The completion record shape is identical across the three policies (fields: principalId, tourVersion, dismissedAt); only the load-time comparison differs. A stored record written under one policy is legal under another (the load-time comparison is what changes).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a completion record written under any of the three policies
acceptanceCriteria.when: the applied policy changes at re-apply time
acceptanceCriteria.then: the record shape is unchanged and the load-time comparison uses the new policy
